title: Foster mother charged in 10-year-old Philadelphia girl's death previously faced abuse allegations, attorney says
text:
Foster mother charged in 10-year-old Philadelphia girl's death previously faced abuse allegations, attorney says - 6abc Philadelphia 
 24/7 Live Philadelphia Pennsylvania New Jersey Delaware Foster mother charged in 10-year-old's death previously faced abuse allegations, attorney says 
 By Leland Pinder Saturday, November 7, 2026 5:08AM 
 The woman accused of murder in the death of her 10-year-old foster child in Philadelphia was previously accused of abusing a child. WPVI PHILADELPHIA (WPVI) -- The woman accused of murder in the death of her 10-year-old foster child in Philadelphia was previously accused of abusing a child.
 The allegations against foster mother Carprice Williams, who is charged with the murder Malayshia Allford, are raising questions about her history as a foster parent and whether she should have been permitted to care for additional children.
 Carprice William, 36, is accused in the "brutal murder" of Malayshia Allford, according to Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner. 
 A criminal complaint alleges Williams abused Allford before her death. According to witnesses cited in the complaint, Williams threw the child down stairs, denied her food and water, and made her wear a weighted vest while walking up and down stairs.
 She then allegedly tried to cover up the murder by texting Allford's phone after she was dead, asking where she was. She then allegedly then sent a response using Allford's phone.
 Malayshia Allford 
 The allegations come as details emerge about a previous abuse case involving another child. According to an attorney involved in that case, the earlier abuse occurred in 2021 and was nearly fatal.
 A lawsuit also detailed Williams' mental health issues and concerns state officials had regarding her care of her biological children.
 Attorney Nadeem Bezar of Kline & Specter said Williams should not have been allowed to foster additional children after the prior case.
 "This child is not supposed to be placed in this home. It makes no sense," Bezar said.
 According to the lawsuit, state officials recommended Williams never foster again after a 4-year-old girl nearly died in her care from severe abuse and malnourishment and a traumatic brain injury.

 Bezar represented the child in a lawsuit against the agencies responsible for overseeing her care. The case was settled this year.
 "How does it happen? It is not supposed to, plain and simple. With what was reported by the prior certifying agency as the reason to closing the home, this is never supposed to happen again," Bezar said.
 Bezar said he had been in the early stages of investigating Allford's case after learning that Pennsylvania DHS found she had been physically and sexually abused in a previous foster home before being placed with Williams last year.
 The placement was managed by Catholic Community Services under the Philadelphia Archdiocese.
 "At this point initially we're looking at the child welfare agencies that certified the homes and the CUA's that are supposed to check on the child," Bezar said.
 Williams also worked as a teacher in the Philadelphia School District. Former parents spoke out to Action News Friday.
 RELATED: What we know about the foster mother charged in death of 10-year-old Malayshia Allford 
 "My kids would always tell me how she'd be mean to them," said Kia Logan of North Philadelphia.
 Another parent, who did not want to be identified, said, "She did a lot in breaking my son's confidence when he was with her, and we are still doing work to rebuild him. I would say she would browbeat him and I very much had to advocate for him."
 The school district said it could not comment on personnel matters when asked for information about Williams' employment. Bezar said he is also examining that aspect of her background.
 "She had access to children so we want to know as much as we can about her," he said.
 Representatives of the Archdiocese of Philadelphia, Tabor Children's Services and Children's Choice did not respond to requests for comment.
